items.title: Arturo Sandoval interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 12, 2023
items.q: He’s a very dear friend. He smoked Fuente like me, and we were having a cigar in his backyard

ctx.x: So what’s the first thing, the very first thing that you do to get started when you get a description of a project and maybe a — not a script but you know here’s the story, here’s what we want to happen.

Okay. I’m going to share with you a secret. When I do things for movies, by the way you know I don’t know if you are aware that I wrote the last two scores for Clint Eastwood. You know? I wrote “The Mule” and “Richard Jewell.” I wrote those two scores for him. They sent me — don’t repeat that — they always send me the script and I read the title. I said oh my goodness, I don’t have time to read a hundred pages of a script. No, no, no, no. Show me the movie, man. Show me the thing. And the way I compose or write…

I talked to him on Friday and I said, “Hey, that was Andy. He said Clint Eastwood was going to call me. What is this?” Okay, the phone rang, I get, the thing is, “Arturo, how are you, this is Clint.” Okay. And then he said, “Arturo I’m doing a movie and there’s a scene there, it’s less than three minutes.” This is a very interesting story. He said, “There’s a scene there that I want you to write a cue, it’s less than three minutes, it’s a big party in the swimming pool of the guy” blah-blah. “And the people are…
